name: text-on-path
title: Text on a path
summary: A sentence that follows a sine wave built with pathExpression, drawn faintly underneath, nudged along and above it with hOffset and vOffset.
prompt: Draw a sentence that follows a sine-wave curve, with the curve drawn faintly underneath.
teaches: Build a sine wave with pathExpression (x and y as functions of a[0]) and name it with id
Draw text along a path with drawTextOnPath(text, path, hOffset, vOffset)
Shift the text along the path with hOffset and off it with vOffset (negative is above)

snippets.note: pathExpression: x = 20 + a[0]*50.93, y = 100 - 45 sin(a[0]), a[0] from 0 to 2π, 96 points
drawTextOnPath on the wave, hOffset 12, vOffset -6

check.describe: The white sentence rises and falls with the faint blue wave, sitting just above it. Resized (260×200, 540×140) the wave spans the width less 20 on each side with an amplitude of 22.5 % of the height, and the sentence follows it.

pitfalls: Build the path with pathExpression (or the op-list path form) rather than an SVG string: Java pads a drawPath SVG string to ~4 KB, and an SVG string in resources.paths becomes an empty path
vOffset is perpendicular to the path and negative lifts the text above it; hOffset is a distance along the path, and text past the path's end is not drawn
Text on a tight curve bunches up on the inside of a bend: keep the curve gentle relative to textSize
A pathExpression with literal scale (50.93 per radian, centre 100) draws for one size only: use componentWidth() / componentHeight() in expressionX / expressionY
